You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜US-Iran Talks Possibly Tomorrow, Hormuz Agreement Signals Emerge; Amazon Completes $50 Billion OpenAI Investment; Palantir Earnings After the Close (August 3, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
Warsh Considers Reducing FOMC Meeting Frequency; September Hike Probability Rises to 73.6%
According to The New York Times , Fed Chair Warsh is considering reducing the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings from the current eight per year. This would break a practice in place since the Volcker era in 1981 and could compress policy transparency and the market’s access to guidance windows.
CME FedWatch data shows the probability of holding rates steady through September has fallen to 26.4%, while the cumulative probability of a 25 bp hike has risen to 73.6%. Through October, the cumulative 25 bp hike probability stands at 62.1% and a 50 bp hike at 17.9%.
Markets continue to digest Warsh’s earlier firm reaffirmation of the 2% inflation target and his downplaying of forward guidance.
Market Impact : Policy-path uncertainty has increased. A reduction in meeting frequency would further lower transparency, providing short-term support for the dollar and pressure on risk-asset valuations. Rising hike expectations weigh on high-valuation tech sectors.
International Commodities
US-Iran Talks Possibly Tomorrow; Hormuz Strait Agreement Signals Emerge; Oil Prices Fall Sharply
President Trump stated on Sunday (Eastern Time) that, at the request of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Iran, he had canceled a planned strike on Iran, noting that “if they had not asked, we would have launched a massive attack last night.” He added that an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz already exists and that a deal on denuclearization is also expected; talks are scheduled to begin tomorrow afternoon (Tuesday morning Beijing time).
Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said negotiations with Oman on safe shipping principles and operational mechanisms for the Strait of Hormuz have entered the final stage and are nearing completion.
OPEC+ agreed to raise September oil production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day.
Market Impact : Expectations of geopolitical de-escalation rapidly compressed the crude risk premium, with WTI falling nearly 5%. Progress on the talks and actual Hormuz shipping conditions remain the key near-term variables for oil prices; a concrete agreement would further ease inflation concerns.
Macroeconomic Policy
US-Japan Coordinated Yen Intervention; Bessent Emphasizes Economic Security Equals National Security
Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed that the US coordinated with Japan last Friday to intervene in the yen market in response to disorderly moves. He stated that the US-Japan alliance is built on both economic and national security and encouraged expanding the scale of the FIMA repo facility.
Trump described the intervention as a symbol of US-Japan friendship and said he expects the US to gain economic benefits, drawing a parallel with the earlier currency-swap arrangement with Argentina.
South Korea plans to inject approximately $14 billion into its sovereign wealth fund for strategic investments in artificial intelligence and related areas.
Market Impact : FX intervention highlights Asian authorities’ heightened focus on currency volatility. Coordinated US-Japan action helps stabilize short-term expectations; Korea’s AI investment plan reflects longer-term industrial positioning.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance
Spot Gold : ~$4,055/oz, +0.28%
Spot Silver : ~$58.3/oz, +1.14%
WTI Crude : ~$80.5/bbl, -4.8%
Brent Crude : ~$79/bbl, -3.17%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : ~99.637, -0.17%
Driver Analysis : US-Iran talk expectations and Hormuz agreement signals rapidly compressed the crude risk premium, with both WTI and Brent falling sharply by nearly 5%, easing near-term inflation concerns. Gold and silver remained relatively resilient amid lower oil prices and a slightly softer dollar; safe-haven demand cooled but did not trigger significant selling. The asset linkage is clear: geopolitical easing → lower oil → marginal cooling of inflation expectations → discussion of a possible softening in Fed hike bets even while probabilities remain elevated. Near-term commodity moves will depend heavily on the outcome of tomorrow’s talks and any concrete agreement.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$63,275, +0.53%
ETH : ~$1,870, +1.04%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.25 trillion, +1%
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$140 million, of which shorts ~$90 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Above the current price (~$63,300), the $63,900–$64,500 zone contains a dense cluster of 100x short liquidations. A break above $64,000 could trigger concentrated short covering and amplify upside. Cumulative short liquidation size above (~$330 million) is slightly below long liquidation size below (~$360 million); long pressure is marginally higher. Short-term focus remains on the $64,000 short-liquidation cluster.

Apple fell more than 7% on softer services results and cautious guidance. The move was driven by “earnings delivery versus guidance concerns”: cloud and AI infrastructure spending received partial validation, while hardware and consumer electronics remained under pressure. Event Overview : Amazon completed its full $50 billion investment in OpenAI, acquiring an approximate 5% stake. It had invested $15 billion in February and committed an additional $35 billion contingent on milestones or an IPO; the latest disclosure confirms all funds have been deployed. AWS cloud revenue grew 37% to $42.2 billion in the second quarter—the fastest pace since 2021. Shares jumped approximately 15.3% on Friday to $271.58, adding substantial market value in a single session. Market Interpretation : Completion of the investment further binds Amazon commercially and equitably with OpenAI while reinforcing AWS as a core cloud-infrastructure provider. Accelerating cloud growth directly validates that large-scale AI capital expenditure is converting into measurable revenue, significantly easing earlier concerns about “excessive investment and an overly long return cycle.” This stood in clear contrast to recent pressure on chip and memory stocks from expectation gaps, and capital rapidly awarded a dual premium for both earnings delivery and strategic positioning. Investment Implication : Cloud and AI monetization has received further validation. Subsequent focus should remain on the pace of investment returns and whether AWS growth can continue to absorb higher levels of capital spending.
